questions.question: How did Aristotle characterize the soul's relationship to a naturally organized body?
questions.reference: the first actuality of a naturally organized body
questions.answer: Aristotle defined the soul as the "first actuality" of a naturally organized body [1]. He argued against its separate existence from the physical body [1], viewing the soul as the organization of the form and matter of a natural being, which allows it to strive for its full actualization [1]. In natural beings, the source of motion required for this full actualization is contained within the being itself [1]. He also held that the soul cannot exist without the body [4].
